steps.path: Any command the assistant runs that needs admin rights
steps.headline: The contract, graded — accept these verdicts?

rows.statement: You type your admin password inside the chat card itself, never a separate system pop-up.
Approving an admin command and entering your password are two separate steps, not one combined action.
The password card can appear after a command has already started, naming the exact step that needs admin rights.
This first version covers only your computer's admin password; other logins (keys, GitHub, SSH) are separate, later projects.
After each admin command finishes, the app makes your computer forget the password, so the next admin step asks again.
Typing your admin password from a paired phone or browser is allowed, with its leftover risks accepted.
When 'sudo' is visibly written in the command, the password is asked right after approval, before anything runs.
Every mode's admin-command card shows the exact command, matches the Full auto stop's look, and has no Always Allow or text below the buttons.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-2/bash-sudo-awaiting-approval--midnight--after.png (approved R2-1) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-sudo-awaiting-approval.png cropped 650x191+72+73 (re-taken via UI_REVIEW_PLANS=admin-password bash scripts/ui-review/run-review.sh) — identical: one 'Stopped before an admin command' band, command shown, Run it / Skip it, nothing below the buttons.

rows.statement: Your password box spans the card, with a show/hide eye and a small Confirm button built into its right side; Enter also confirms.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-4/bash-sudo-password--midnight--after.png (approved R4-1) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-sudo-password.png cropped 650x197+72+73 — identical: full-width password field, eye + small Confirm built into its right side, no subtext line.

rows.statement: A wrong password shows a yellow warning banner saying how many tries remain, and clears the box for your next try.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-2/bash-sudo-password-wrong--midnight--after.png (approved R2-4) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-sudo-password-wrong.png cropped 650x260+72+73 — the yellow 'Wrong password' banner with '2 tries left.' is present, box is empty for the next try; only the since-approved R3-1/R4-1 layout changes below it (no subtext, inline Confirm) differ, which is expected and itself verified under R8.

rows.statement: Before your last try, the same yellow banner warns that another wrong password may lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-2/bash-sudo-password-last-try--midnight--after.png (approved R2-5) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-sudo-password-last-try.png cropped 650x260+72+73 — identical banner text: '1 try left. Another wrong one may lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes.'

rows.statement: When a script asks for your password partway through, a highlighted box names the script and says to type only if you expected it.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-2/bash-script-password-midway--midnight--after.png (approved R2-6) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-script-password-midway.png cropped 650x260+72+73 — identical highlighted box: 'Asked partway through install.sh' + 'Only type your password if you expected this step.'

rows.statement: A command still running with admin rights shows a 'Running as admin' strip with how long it's run and a Stop button, even when folded.
rows.evidence: images/admin-password.review-3/bash-sudo-running-as-admin--midnight--after.png (approved R3-2) vs runs/built/shots-admin-password/midnight/bash-sudo-running-as-admin.png cropped 650x138+72+73 — identical: 'Running as admin · 12m 18s' strip with Stop button, shown on the folded/background card.

rows.statement: Your admin password is never saved, never shown to the assistant, and never written into chat history.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/chat-reducer-admin-password.test.ts (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: it asserts PASSWORD_REQUEST/PASSWORD_RESOLVED never carry a password field through the reducer or chat state (top-level and nested-under-Task cases), and hook-dispatcher's PasswordRequest/PasswordResolved mapping is asserted 'with no password field ever read' — matches the row (never saved, never shown to the assistant, never written into chat history).

rows.statement: The password card's wording is always the app's own, never text a command supplies.
Your password is only ever handed to your computer's genuine admin program, never to something faking it.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/askpass-verify.test.ts (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: verifyAskpassPeer is driven through a fake /proc (exe path, cmdline, environ, ppid, start-time, tracer pid, pidfd, filesystem stat chain) covering every refusal reason and the accept path, including the TOCTOU pid-recycling race — matches the row (password only ever handed to genuine sudo).

rows.statement: Full auto still stops for every admin command, and a helper's admin request shows on your card labeled with its name.
Three wrong passwords in a row can lock you out of admin actions for about 10 minutes, and you're warned before the last try.
Every step waits for you with no time limit; the approval card's Skip, or closing the session, stops the command.
This is for Mac and Linux; Windows keeps its own pop-up and phones still can't run admin commands.
Where the password card isn't available (Macs, for now), an approved command still runs if no password is needed; the assistant knows why otherwise.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/harness-session-loop.test.ts — 145 passed, 0 failed, exit 0 (commit 69f405a54 strengthened the guard). Read the test: 'passwordless sudo still runs after approval when adminPasswordService is unset entirely (F1)' now asserts BOTH halves of the row inside the same case — the command still runs with no adminPasswordService wired (askUser called once, bash.calls.length === 1), AND, after setAdminPasswordAvailable(false), BashTool.description (the real getter installed at desktop/src/main/harness/tools/bash.ts:1137, reading the same isAdminPasswordAvailable() flag production reads) contains '`sudo` only works here when the command needs no password (NOPASSWD)' and no longer contains 'the user types their admin password in a card' — the exact 'assistant knows why otherwise' half, now checked against the real tool object rather than a duplicated string. Guard now matches the row's full statement.

rows.statement: An admin command that runs and finishes normally no longer leaves a permanent entry sitting in memory for your session.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/shell-registry.test.ts (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: 'clearAccepted() removes an acceptance directly, for a call that never reaches ShellRegistry at all' (the exact leak path code review F2 named — a foreground-only run's markAdmin() entry that onExit() never clears) plus 'clearAccepted() for a toolUseId that was never marked is a no-op' and 'a SECOND run for the same toolCallId does not inherit acceptedToolCallIds after the first exited and cleared it' — matches the row, and clearAccepted() is wired into production at desktop/src/main/harness/tools/bash.ts:1112.

rows.statement: The up-front password ask reads a command's quoting the same way on every platform, instead of silently disagreeing with the approval check.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/admin-command.test.ts (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: 'tokenizes with the SAME platform rule as adminCommandVerdict, given the same ctx (F3)' explicitly reproduces the code review's platform-mismatch finding and asserts visibleSudoLines and adminCommandVerdict now agree — matches the row (up-front ask reads quoting the same way as the approval check, on every platform).

rows.statement: A brand-new password ask always starts with an empty, hidden box, even at the same tries-left count as before.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/AdminPasswordPrompt.test.tsx (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: describe('AdminPasswordPrompt — the field resets for a genuinely new ask (F4)') / 'clears the typed value and hides the eye toggle when requestId changes, even at the SAME triesLeft' — exactly the row's statement.

rows.statement: Pressing Enter after typing your password submits it, the same as clicking Confirm.
rows.evidence: npx vitest run youcoded/desktop/tests/AdminPasswordPrompt.test.tsx (part of a 6-file run) — 366 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. Read the file: describe('AdminPasswordPrompt — Enter submits like Confirm') / 'fires onSubmit exactly once when Enter is pressed in a non-empty field' plus the empty-field no-op and Shift+Enter no-op cases — exactly the row's statement.
